chapters.title: Think like a photographer
chapters.text: Every Auto Optimize choice is a photographer's decision, made in code.

chapters.title: Shutter vs. ISO
chapters.text: With a fixed aperture, exposure trades shutter for ISO: fast freezes motion but adds noise, slow blurs it.

chapters.title: Meter for the subject
chapters.text: Averaging the frame turns a backlit face into a silhouette. Meter for the face, and let the window blow out.

chapters.title: Protect the highlights
chapters.text: Clipped highlights hold no data. Crushed shadows can be lifted, with some noise. So guard the highlights first.

chapters.title: Tone curves make the look
chapters.text: Most pro looks are tone curves. An S-curve adds contrast; lifted blacks and soft highlights feel like film.

chapters.title: White balance has two axes
chapters.text: White balance has two axes: blue to amber, and green to magenta. A gray card reads neutral when it's right.

chapters.title: Protect skin tones
chapters.text: Skin of every complexion sits near one line. Push a global grade and faces drift magenta, so protect that range.

chapters.title: Read the light
chapters.text: Front light is flat, side light shows texture, back light makes a rim. Small sources light hard, large ones soft.

chapters.title: Composition basics
chapters.text: Rule of thirds, a level horizon, leading lines and headroom. Each one makes a good guide overlay.

chapters.title: Know the pipeline
chapters.text: Apple's ISP processes every frame before your code sees it. Shoot RAW alongside to see what it did.

chapters.title: Build a hard-scene test set
chapters.text: Test every change on the scenes that break cameras, then shoot manually for a week. That habit is what Auto Optimize automates.
